subject: Emotions
title: Aesthetic Disgust
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Aesthetic Disgust.

hook.text: Trypophobia—fear of small holes—affects 15% of people. Lotus pods and honeycombs trigger real nausea.

buildup.text: There's no pathogen in a lotus pod. Yet the clustered holes trigger the same brain pathway as rot.

discovery.text: Researchers think the pattern resembles diseased skin. The brain misreads it as a parasite signal.

twist.text: Aesthetic disgust means some art, design, and architecture can trigger physical nausea in viewers.

climax.text: Horror filmmakers exploit this. Textures that mimic disease cues create visceral audience reactions.

punchline.text: Your brain sees danger in patterns, not just substances.
